title: Evaluation of a normalized derived comparison on successive resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A',\mathcal B,\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and assume every complex in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$ admits a K-injective resolution (a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes). Let $r:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ and $s:\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ be exact additive functors, applied degreewise and descended to the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $Fr=sG$ on objects and morphisms. Let $RF,RG$ be their total right derived functors [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], with units $\eta^F,\eta^G$, and let
$$\beta:RF\circ r\xrightarrow{\sim}s\circ RG$$
be a supplied natural isomorphism. Suppose it is normalized as follows: for any K-injective $J$ in $\mathcal A'$ and any K-injective resolution $v:rJ\to T$ in $\mathcal A$, $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)$ is invertible and
$$(s\eta^G_J)^{-1}\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}J}\circ(c^F_v)^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)^{-1},$$
where $c^F_v:RF(Q_{\mathcal A}(rJ))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal B}(FT)$ is the canonical resolution identification [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]; all exact-functor localization identifications are understood. Let $N$ be any complex in $\mathcal A'$, let $u:N\to J$ be a K-injective resolution, and let $v:rJ\to T$ be a K-injective resolution. Put $w=v\circ r(u):rN\to T$, another K-injective resolution since $r$ is exact. Under the resolution identifications $c^F_w$ and $s(c^G_u)$ of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], the comparison at $N$ is
$$s(c^G_u)\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}N}\circ(c^F_w)^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)^{-1}:Q_{\mathcal B}(FT)\longrightarrow Q_{\mathcal B}(F(rJ))=Q_{\mathcal B}(sGJ).$$
The equality is valid for every such $u,v$, with the canonical changes of resolution in [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]; it does not assume that $rJ$ is K-injective.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined): K-injective computation of total right derived functors; the stated arbitrary-resolution/naturality consequence is an agent formulation of this computation, not a verbatim Stacks lemma.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $r(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $w=v\circ r(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism with K-injective target $T$, so is a K-injective resolution. Write $q=Q_{\mathcal A'}u$ and $a=Q_{\mathcal A}(r(u))$; the localization identifications identify $a$ with $r(q)$. The defining formula for resolution identifications in [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], applied to $F$ with resolutions $v,w$ and to $G$ with resolution $u$, gives
$$c^F_w=(\eta^F_T)^{-1}RF(Q_{\mathcal A}w)=c^F_v\circ RF(a),\qquad c^G_u=(\eta^G_J)^{-1}\circ RG(q).$$
All these maps are isomorphisms: $q,a$ are localized quasi-isomorphisms, $T,J$ are K-injective, and the cited lemma gives invertibility of their derived units. In particular
$$(c^F_w)^{-1}=RF(a)^{-1}\circ(c^F_v)^{-1}.$$

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation lemma; explicit naturality and cancellation argument by Q112.

proof.text:
Naturality of the supplied natural isomorphism $\beta$ at $q$ says
$$s(RG(q))\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}N}=\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}J}\circ RF(a).$$
Substitute the two formulas from step 1 and use functoriality of $s$, associativity, and $RF(a)\circ RF(a)^{-1}=1$. This gives the explicit equality
$$\begin{aligned}s(c^G_u)\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}N}\circ(c^F_w)^{-1}
&=(s\eta^G_J)^{-1}\circ s(RG(q))\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}N}\circ RF(a)^{-1}\circ(c^F_v)^{-1}\\
&=(s\eta^G_J)^{-1}\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}J}\circ(c^F_v)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation lemma; explicit naturality and cancellation argument by Q112.

proof.text: The complex $J$ is K-injective and $v:rJ\to T$ is the chosen K-injective resolution, exactly the two hypotheses in the supplied normalization. That normalization identifies the last expression of step 2 with $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)^{-1}$. Its target is $Q_{\mathcal B}(F(rJ))=Q_{\mathcal B}(sGJ)$ because $Fr=sG$ on complexes. This proves the displayed assertion for the arbitrary pair $u,v$; no K-injectivity of $rJ$ was used. Invertibility of $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)$ is used only as the explicit normalization hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), via the cited K-injective computation lemma; explicit naturality and cancellation argument by Q112.

proof.text:
To check the last compatibility clause, take two choices $u_i:N\to J_i$, $v_i:rJ_i\to T_i$, and put $w_i=v_i r(u_i)$ and $L_i=s(c^G_{u_i})\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}N}(c^F_{w_i})^{-1}$ for $i=1,2$. By the resolution-transition clause of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], the canonical changes at the source and target are respectively
$$d_F=c^F_{w_2}(c^F_{w_1})^{-1},\qquad d_G=s(c^G_{u_2}(c^G_{u_1})^{-1}).$$
Associativity and cancellation give $L_2=d_G\circ L_1\circ d_F^{-1}$. Since step 3 identifies $L_i=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv_i)^{-1}$, this is precisely the compatibility of the asserted arrows with both canonical changes of resolution. The cited lemma gives the cocycle identities for these changes, so the same equation is consistent for three or more choices.
